key_results: Bacterial transcription factors and periplasmic binding proteins (conserved fold, same sugar ligands) possess distinct energetic blueprints; rational redesign yielded synthetic transcription factors with predicted ligand-induced outputs
comments: Innovative application of ensemble energetics to protein engineering, though the causal link between energetic differences and functional specialization could be more rigorously validated.

Rational protein redesign for synthetic transcription factors

hypotheses.hypothesis: Energy-driven engineering of protein folds enables tunable, predictable functional outputs
hypotheses.result: Synthetic transcription factors exhibited theoretically anticipated ligand-induced transcriptional responses
